issues.legal_issue: A subtenant may acquire direct tenancy under a later tenancy law even when an ejectment suit against the subtenant was pending under the repealed law.
material_facts: An ejectment suit against a subtenant was pending when a new tenancy law repealed the law governing the suit, and no eviction decree or order had been made.
While the suit remained pending, the subtenant gave the required notice and applied to the rent authority for recognition as a direct tenant under the superior landlord.
The rent authority declared the subtenant a direct tenant, and the trial court found that the landlord-and-tenant relationship between the parties to the ejectment suit had ceased.
issues.conclusion: The pending ejectment suit remained governed by the repealed law, but the savings provision did not prevent the subtenant from acquiring the new law’s right to direct tenancy. The relationship between the parties ceased when the rent authority made its declaration.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 16(2) and 16(3) of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1956, a subtenant could, after the prescribed notice and application, be declared a tenant directly under the superior landlord. Section 2(h) included a person continuing in possession until an eviction decree or order was made. Section 40 saved pending proceedings as if the repealed Act remained in force, but did not deny a subtenant the distinct new right conferred by the 1956 Act.

rule.if: pending_ejectment_proceeding and subtenant_in_possession and no_eviction_order and new_law_allows_direct_tenancy and rent_authority_declared_direct_tenancy

predicates.pending_ejectment_proceeding: An ejectment proceeding against a subtenant was pending when the governing law changed.
predicates.subtenant_in_possession: The subtenant continued in possession of the premises.
predicates.no_eviction_order: No eviction decree or order had been made against the subtenant when the direct-tenancy declaration was made.
predicates.new_law_allows_direct_tenancy: A law in force gave a subtenant a procedure to become a tenant directly under the superior landlord.
predicates.rent_authority_declared_direct_tenancy: The rent authority declared the subtenant to be a direct tenant under the superior landlord.
predicates.subtenant_becomes_direct_tenant: The subtenant becomes a tenant directly under the superior landlord.

issues.definition: When an ejectment proceeding is pending but no eviction order has been made, a subtenant in possession becomes a direct tenant if the applicable new law permits that status and the rent authority declares it.

issues.legal_issue: The doctrine of lis pendens does not prevent a statutory change in the landlord-and-tenant relationship that is not a transfer of property by a party to the pending suit.
material_facts: An ejectment suit concerning the premises was pending when the subtenant sought recognition as a direct tenant under the new tenancy law.
The rent authority’s order extinguished the original tenant’s interest in the sublet portion and gave the subtenant a direct tenancy under the superior landlord.
The change in the parties’ relationship resulted from the operation of the law and the rent authority’s order, not from a transfer of property by a party to the suit.
issues.conclusion: The doctrine of lis pendens did not apply to the direct-tenancy order and did not prevent that order from affecting the pending ejectment suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, concerns a party’s transfer or other dealing with disputed property during pending litigation that affects another party’s rights under the eventual decree or order. Section 5 defines a transfer of property as an act by which a living person conveys property to another. Applying Bellamy v. Sabine, quoted with approval in Faiyaz Husain Khan v. Munshi Prag Narain, the Court explained that a statutory alteration of landlord-and-tenant rights is not an alienation by a party and does not attract lis pendens.

rule.if: pending_property_suit and statutory_change_in_tenancy_relationship and not party_transferred_property

predicates.pending_property_suit: A suit concerning rights in property was pending.
predicates.statutory_change_in_tenancy_relationship: A law and an order made under it altered the landlord-and-tenant relationship concerning the property.
predicates.party_transferred_property: A party to the pending suit conveyed or otherwise transferred the disputed property during the suit.
predicates.lis_pendens_does_not_bar_statutory_chang: The doctrine of lis pendens does not prevent the statutory change from taking effect.

issues.definition: If a law and an order under it alter the tenancy relationship during a property suit without a party transferring the property, lis pendens does not bar that change.
